thread.title: Roku rockets 6% as Silicon Valley stocks shrug off big Dow drop

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Roku rockets 6% as Silicon Valley stocks shrug off big Dow drop
text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 20, 2018, 1:49pm PST Updated Feb 20, 2018, 2:02pm PST It was another rough day for U.S. equities, but Silicon Valley stocks emerged relatively unscathed. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 250 on Tuesday, ending a six-day winning streak , as Walmart (NYSE: WMT) shares posted their worst day in 30 years. The retail giant plummeted more than 10 percent on a major earnings miss. Facing more aggressive competition from Amazon.com (NASDAQ: AMZN) than ever before, Walmart said Tuesday that it would invest heavily in growing its e-commerce platform . Among Silicon Valley stocks, Roku (NASDAQ: ROKU) leapt to the top of the local ranks as it closed up 6.34 percent. The Los Gatos-based company reports fourth-quarter earnings after the closing bell on Wednesday. It wasn’t immediately clear what caused the latest pop, but the stock has been exceptionally volatile since its September 2017 arrival on Wall Street. Los Gatos-based Roku was the top-performing Silicon Valley IPO last year and shares are still up more than 223 percent from their debut price. The other top-performing local stocks on Tuesday: • Cypress Semiconductor (NASDAQ: CY) jumped 4.02 percent after approving an 11 cent quarterly cash dividend . • Credit score company Fair Isaac Corp. (NYSE: FICO) gained 3.36 percent. • Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) rose 3.15 percent, making it the top performer on the Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Tech index . • Xilinx (NASDAQ: XLNX) closed up 3.13 percent. The worst performers were: • Logitech International S.A. (NASDAQ: LOGI) slipped 2.5 percent. • SunPower Corp. (NASDAQ: SPWR) fell 1.96 percent, continuing their slide from Friday . Investors are worried about the impact of President Trump's solar tariffs. • Essex Property Trust (NYSE: ESS) declined 1.85 percent. • Netgear (NASDAQ: NTGR) dropped 1.85 percent. The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Tech Index of the 13 largest Silicon Valley tech stocks declined 0.15 percent. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG), Adobe Systems (NASDAQ: ADBE) and eBay (NASDAQ: EBAY) were the index's top performers. Symantec Corp. (NASDAQ: SYMC), Oracle Corp. (NASDAQ: ORCL), Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) and Cisco Systems (CSCO) were its worst performers. Its biggest member, Apple , (NASDAQ: AAPL) slipped 0.34 percent. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 20, 2018, 1:49pm PST Updated Feb 20, 2018, 2:02pm PST Related Content
